objects.description: Enumeration of AST node kinds used in the regex parser. Guides which union member in cregex_node_t is active (character, class, quantifier, concatenation, alternation, anchors, capture, etc.).

AST node for the regex syntax tree. The 'type' selects which anonymous struct in the union is valid: character (ch), character class ranges (from/to), quantifier (nmin, nmax, greedy, quantified), binary composition (left/right), or capture (captured). Nodes are typically produced by cregex_parse and freed with cregex_parse_free. Unknown memory ownership details beyond that.
Enumeration of VM opcodes for the compiled regex program: character and class matches, control flow (split/jump), assertions for begin/end, save slots, and terminal match.
Bitset representing a character class over unsigned char domain. Size is enough to cover UCHAR_MAX. Use helper inlines cregex_char_class_contains and cregex_char_class_add to query/mutate bits.

Instruction node in the compiled regex program. The opcode selects which union member is active: character (ch), character class bitset (klass), control-flow pointers (first/second/target), or save slot index (save). Instances are created as part of cregex_program_t by cregex_compile_node.

Compiled regex program consisting of a count and a flexible array of cregex_program_instr_t. Constructed by cregex_compile_node, executed by cregex_program_run, and freed with cregex_compile_free. Ownership/lifetime is managed by the caller after construction.

functions.name: cregex_program_run
functions.signature: int cregex_program_run(const cregex_program_t *program, const char *string, const char **matches, int nmatches);
functions.description: Execute a compiled regex program against a C string. Intended to run the VM over the provided input and optionally collect match information in the matches array. Return value semantics (e.g., success/failure or count) are not documented in this header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: program must point to a valid compiled program obtained from cregex_compile_node.
string must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
nmatches must be non-negative.

If nmatches > 0, matches should reference writable storage for at least nmatches const char* entries; if no match data is desired, matches may be NULL only when nmatches == 0 (inferred from common patterns; exact behavior is not documented).
The lifetime of string must outlive the call (pointers stored into matches, if any, will reference positions within string; exact format/semantics are not documented).

functions.name: cregex_compile_node
functions.description: Compile a parsed regex AST (root) into an executable program representation suitable for cregex_program_run. Returns a heap-allocated program object or NULL on failure (return-on-failure behavior is inferred; not explicitly documented).
requirements: root must be a valid parse tree produced by cregex_parse and must remain alive during compilation.
The returned program must be freed with cregex_compile_free to avoid leaks.
Do not pass NULL for root; behavior is not documented for NULL.

functions.name: cregex_compile_free
functions.description: Free a program previously created by cregex_compile_node. Releases any resources owned by the compiled program.
requirements: program must be a pointer previously returned by cregex_compile_node and not already freed.
program must not be NULL unless the implementation explicitly documents NULL-tolerant free (not documented here).
After this call, program must not be used.

functions.name: cregex_parse
functions.description: Parse a regex pattern string into an abstract syntax tree (AST) rooted at a cregex_node_t. The returned tree can be compiled with cregex_compile_node. Error signaling (e.g., NULL on failure) is not explicitly documented but is typical; exact details are unknown.
requirements: pattern must be a valid, null-terminated C string containing the regex to parse.
The returned AST must be freed with cregex_parse_free when no longer needed.
Do not pass NULL for pattern; behavior is not documented for NULL.

functions.name: cregex_parse_free
functions.description: Free a parsed regex AST previously allocated by cregex_parse. Releases all nodes anchored at root.
requirements: root must be a pointer previously returned by cregex_parse and not already freed.
root must not be NULL unless the implementation explicitly documents NULL-tolerant free (not documented here).
After this call, root and any pointers into the tree must not be used.

functions.name: cregex_char_class_contains
functions.signature: static inline int cregex_char_class_contains(const cregex_char_class klass, int ch);
functions.description: Return nonzero if character code ch is present in the character class bitset klass; otherwise return 0. Intended for quick membership tests in a pre-initialized cregex_char_class.
requirements: klass must reference a valid cregex_char_class buffer (array of (UCHAR_MAX + CHAR_BIT - 1) / CHAR_BIT bytes).
klass should be initialized (typically zeroed) before use; otherwise results are undefined due to uninitialized bits (inferred from bitset semantics).
ch must be in the range 0..UCHAR_MAX; passing values outside this range will index outside the bitset storage.

functions.name: cregex_char_class_add
functions.signature: static inline int cregex_char_class_add(cregex_char_class klass, int ch);
functions.description: Set the bit corresponding to character code ch in the character class bitset klass (add ch to the class) and return ch. Used to construct character classes.
requirements: klass must reference a valid, writable cregex_char_class buffer (array of (UCHAR_MAX + CHAR_BIT - 1) / CHAR_BIT bytes).
klass should be initialized (typically zeroed) before first addition to ensure only intended bits are set (inferred from bitset semantics).
ch must be in the range 0..UCHAR_MAX; values outside this range will index outside the bitset storage.
klass must not be const; the buffer must be mutable.

data_types.description: A null-terminated C string containing a regex pattern to be parsed. May include literals, character classes (e.g., [a-z]), quantifiers (*, +, ?, {m,n}), grouping and captures (parentheses), alternation (|), anchors (^, $), and escape sequences. It is arbitrary text interpreted as a regex grammar, not plain data.

A generic null-terminated C string containing arbitrary bytes/text with no required structure. Used as input to matching functions where the content is treated as plain text to be searched or matched against (not parsed as a format).

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for interesting arbitrary text strings intended to be consumed as C strings
# by cregex_program_run as the input to match against. We try to cover a broad range
# of text characteristics: ASCII, unicode-like UTF-8 sequences, long/short, newlines,
# repeated patterns, edge characters, and embedded NUL avoidance (final buffer is a
# Python bytes blob; fuzzer infra will make it a std::string, so internal NUL bytes are
# allowed but may truncate depending on how the target interprets it; since the target
# uses C strings, we avoid embedding NUL before the end to maximize coverage of the
# full buffer in C-string APIs).

MAX_LEN = 1024  # keep under 4096 total

ASCII_PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127) if c != 0)
WHITESPACE = '\t \r\n\v\f'
PUNCT = string.punctuation
DIGITS = string.digits
LETTERS = string.ascii_letters
ESCAPES = ['\\n', '\\r', '\\t', '\\f', '\\v', '\\0', '\\\\']

# Some common words and tokens that help regex engines exercise character classes,
# anchors, word boundaries, etc.
DICTIONARY = [
    'hello', 'world', 'test', 'regex', 'cregex', 'alpha', 'beta', 'gamma', 'delta',
    'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', 'five', 'zero', 'nine',
    'email@example.com', 'user_name', 'CamelCase', 'snake_case', 'kebab-case',
    'UPPER', 'lower', 'MiXeD', '12345', '0000', '9999',
    'BEGIN', 'END', 'start', 'finish', 'match', 'nomatch',
]

# Some UTF-8 sequences to exercise any byte-class handling and dot/any-character logic
UTF8_SNIPPETS = [
    'π', 'μ', '✓', '❤', 'é', 'ä', 'ö', 'ü', 'ñ', 'Ж', '漢字', 'ひらがな', '한글', '😀',
]

# Repetition building blocks to trigger greedy vs non-greedy behavior in the program
REPEAT_BLOCKS = [
    'a', 'b', 'ab', 'abc', 'xyz', '0', '1', '01', '.', '*', '+', '?', '[abc]', '(foo)'
]

BOUNDARY_CHUNKS = [
    '', ' ', '\n', '\r\n', '\t', '\v', '\f', '--', '::', '##', '__', '  ', '   ',
]

EDGE_BYTE_RUNS = [
    bytes([i for i in range(1, 32) if i != 0]).decode('latin1', 'ignore'),  # control chars sans NUL
    ''.join(chr(i) for i in range(127, 160)),  # DEL and C1 controls
]

START_END_MARKERS = [
    '^start', 'end$', '^', '$', '\nstart', 'end\n', '[', ']', '(', ')', '{', '}',
]

URL_LIKE = [
    'http://example.com/path?query=1#frag',
    'https://sub.domain.tld:8080/a/b/c',
]

PATHS = [
    '/usr/bin/env', 'C:/Windows/System32', './relative/path', '../up/one',
]

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List):
    return arr[rng.randrange(len(arr))]

def _repeat(rng: random.Random, s: str, min_n: int, max_n: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_n, max_n)
    return s * n

def _make_repeated_patterns(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)):
        blk = _rand_choice(rng, REPEAT_BLOCKS)
        parts.append(_repeat(rng, blk, 1, 50))
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, BOUNDARY_CHUNKS))
    return ''.join(parts)

def _make_dictionary_line(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    words = [
        _rand_choice(rng, DICTIONARY + UTF8_SNIPPETS),
        _rand_choice(rng, DICTIONARY + UTF8_SNIPPETS),
        _rand_choice(rng, DICTIONARY + UTF8_SNIPPETS),
    ]
    sep = _rand_choice(rng, [' ', '\t', ',', ';', ':', '-', '_'])
    return sep.join(words)

def _make_mixed_content(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    builders = [
        lambda: _make_dictionary_line(rng),
        lambda: _make_repeated_patterns(rng),
        lambda: _rand_choice(rng, URL_LIKE),
        lambda: _rand_choice(rng, PATHS),
        lambda: _rand_choice(rng, START_END_MARKERS),
        lambda: _rand_choice(rng, EDGE_BYTE_RUNS),
        lambda: ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 40))),
        lambda: ''.join(rng.choice(WHITESPACE) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10))),
        lambda: ''.join(_rand_choice(rng, UTF8_SNIPPETS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10))),
        lambda: ''.join(_rand_choice(rng, ESCAPES) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))),
        lambda: ''.join(rng.choice(LETTERS + DIGITS + PUNCT) for _ in range(rng.randint(10, 60))),
    ]
    s = []
    while sum(len(x) for x in s) < target_len:
        s.append(_rand_choice(rng, builders)())
        # add newlines to create multi-line inputs for ^ and $ assertions
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s.append('\n')
    return ''.join(s)

def _trim_to_cstring_safe(s: str, max_len: int) -> str:
    # Avoid internal NUL to ensure full string is visible to C API; strip or replace with space
    s = s.replace('\x00', ' ')
    # Hard limit
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]
    # Ensure not ending with a backslash that could interact with escape-aware matchers
    if s.endswith('\\'):
        s += ' '
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Select a strategy to shape the input
    strategy = rng.randrange(6)

    if strategy == 0:
        # Short lines with boundaries and punctuation
        parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8)):
            parts.append(_make_dictionary_line(rng))
            parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, ['\n', '\r\n']))
        s = ''.join(parts)
    elif strategy == 1:
        # Heavily repeated patterns
        s = _make_repeated_patterns(rng)
    elif strategy == 2:
        # Mixed content up to a medium length
        s = _make_mixed_content(rng, rng.randint(64, 512))
    elif strategy == 3:
        # Word-like tokens separated by whitespace and punctuation
        tokens = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(10, 100)):
            tok = ''.join(rng.choice(LETTERS + DIGITS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 12)))
            tokens.append(tok)
        sep_choices = [' ', '\t', ',', ';', '.', ':', '/', '\\', '-', '_']
        s = ''.join(t + _rand_choice(rng, sep_choices) for t in tokens)
    elif strategy == 4:
        # Many lines to exercise anchors
        lines = []
        for i in range(rng.randint(5, 200)):
            prefix = '^' if rng.random() < 0.1 else ''
            suffix = '$' if rng.random() < 0.1 else ''
            body = ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 60)))
            lines.append(prefix + body + suffix)
        s = '\n'.join(lines)
    else:
        # UTF-8 heavy content with interspersed ASCII
        chunks = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(10, 80)):
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                chunks.append(_rand_choice(rng, UTF8_SNIPPETS))
            else:
                chunks.append(''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))))
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                chunks.append('\n')
        s = ''.join(chunks)

    # Augment with some boundary markers at start/end to exercise ^ and $
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = _rand_choice(rng, START_END_MARKERS) + s
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = s + _rand_choice(rng, START_END_MARKERS)

    # Ensure size and C-string friendliness
    s = _trim_to_cstring_safe(s, MAX_LEN)

    # Encode to bytes. Use UTF-8; replace errors so we always return bytes.
    return s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
